name: AI-Native SDLC — stephen8n
description: Anthropic's six-stage AI-native SDLC (Plan, Design, Build, Test, Deploy, Maintain) with a seventh stage, Assess, before Design. The stephen8n version: one human, Stephen, accepts every gate; agents draft and never approve; Git is the only record; nothing an agent does changes a running machine. Derived from the Mace-governed template with DAD05, the Software Design Authority, the Information Steward and the client obligations removed, and the estate's own traps written in.
regulatoryFramework: UK GDPR where personal data is handled
Third-party or client IP terms where such material is in scope (kept out of Git, gitignored, never in fixtures)
NIST AI RMF used as a checklist, not a mandate

git.branchProtection: PR required on main; the agent that authored a PR is never its approver; Stephen merges

machines: Mac Mini (projects, pm2, Caddy, cloudflared, Postgres 5433)
estate.deploy: Human-only. pm2 restart, Caddy, cloudflared, az, wrangler and portal builds are run by Stephen
traps: auto-update.sh on the Mini pulls and restarts every Wednesday 04:00: a branch left checked out ships itself

secrets.rule: Never in Git, never in an issue, never in a prompt

informationManagement.standard: Version-controlled artefact chain (Anthropic AI-native SDLC), stephen8n governed
artefactChain: plan.md, then code — Build — Stephen (human) corrects plan.md before any code is written
Test results and REVIEW.md findings — Test — Nobody. Findings inform; a failing review blocks merge
Merged PR, tag, release notes — Deploy — Stephen (human) merges and deploys
bands.yaml, then a new intent.md — Maintain — Stephen (human) triages

controls.hooks: PreToolUse hooks in .claude/settings.json allow, ask or block. Blocked outright for agents: pm2, launchctl, caddy, cloudflared, az, wrangler, git push --force, rm -rf outside the worktree, any write under ~/secrets.
controls.branchProtection: PR required on main; author is never approver; Stephen merges.
controls.worktrees: Agents work in git worktrees on a branch per issue; the checked-out branch on the Mini stays main because auto-update.sh ships it.
controls.clientMaterial: Fixtures, exports and inventories holding third-party or client material live in gitignored folders and are named in ai-risk-assessment.md.

changeGovernance.reference: stephen8n agentic change rules v1, 2026-09-05, derived from the Mace Agentic Change Governance page
changeGovernance.envelope: The parameters accepted at Gate 2 (Assess): the data the agents may touch, the tools they may call, the people they may serve, the writes they may make, the model version they run, and the money they may spend per month. Gate 2 is the only gate that can change the envelope; every other gate operates inside it.

changeClasses.standard: Stays inside the envelope. Agents draft, Stephen accepts each gate in turn. No reassessment.
changeClasses.normal: Would extend the envelope on any axis. Stephen reassesses (a new ai-risk-assessment.md is merged), then the gates run.
changeClasses.emergency: Service failing or unsafe. Stephen fixes forward or rolls back himself and writes it up within a week as a new intent.md.
changeClasses.prohibited: Outside the envelope with no accepted reassessment, or any agent action that changes a running machine, deploys, or moves client material into Git. Nobody accepts it; hooks refuse it.

kindsOfChange.A: Code and configuration in Git. Reversible by revert or by re-deploying the previous tag.
kindsOfChange.B: Data or schema. Reversible only if the migration has a down path or a backup was taken first; the plan must say which.
kindsOfChange.C: An external write (email, SharePoint, a tenant, a payment, a public page). Not reversible; compensating action only. Human-only unless the envelope names it.

rollbackAndFixForward: Safe state is named in ai-risk-assessment.md before design starts.
Every deployable is a tag; rollback is re-deploying the previous tag and is pre-authorised by Gate 2.
Fix forward is allowed for emergencies only and is written up within a week.
Kind C changes have a compensating action written in plan.md before they are made.
The rollback command is in the release notes before the merge.
A rollback is itself recorded as a release.

obligations.note: Named in the assessment with its lawful basis, or a written statement that none is in scope
Kept out of Git by .gitignore; the Verification Agent scans for it on every PR
Provider, region and what leaves the machine, stated per call type
Per-agent monthly budget in Paperxlip is the control; the Maintain Agent's bands watch it
~/secrets only; never in Git, issues or prompts
Any output that could gate a decision about a person is flagged and a human makes the decision

rules.rule: Every product has a merged ai-risk-assessment.md stating its envelope before design starts, and that assessment defines a standard change for it.
Each gate is accepted by Stephen and Git records it. An agent never approves an artefact, its own or another agent's.
Any change that would extend the envelope on any axis is reassessed before it is built.
No agent runs a command that changes a running machine or a live service. Deploys, restarts, DNS, tunnels and cloud changes are Stephen's.
Fixtures, exports, inventories and anything holding client or third-party material are gitignored and never committed, and the assessment names them.
Every deployable is a tag. If it cannot be named by version it cannot be rolled back and it is not finished.
Agents work on a branch in a worktree. The checked-out branch on the Mini stays main.
Kind C external writes are human-only unless the envelope names them, and always have a compensating action written first.
Artefacts are short. A one-page assessment that is read beats a ten-page one that is not.
A monitoring finding re-enters the pipeline as intent.md, not as a direct fix.
Agent definitions (instructions, tools, model pin, budget) are versioned with the code.
The weekly delivery summary names every gate waiting on Stephen and for how long.
